newsitem.title: CONGO: Witchcraft killings of elderly on rise in Congo.
newsitem.headline: Witchcraft killings of elderly on rise in Congo.

text.p: More than 40 elderly people accused of witchcraft have been put to death, sometimes by burning, by members of their family in Congo this year, a Congolese human rights group said on Tuesday.

Officials at the Congolese Human Rights Observatory (OCDH), in comments coinciding with world day for the aged, added that most of the deaths were in the north of the Central African oil-producing country and that such killings were on the rise.

In a separate statement, the Congolese Society for the Aged (SCG), a non-governmental organisation working to protect old people, said that more than 60 people had been burnt or buried alive after similar accusations between 1990 and 1996.
Some sources say the figures are a conservative estimate.

Such killings are common in remote rural corners of Africa where death in a family is often blamed on witchcraft. Old people, often deemed as having outlived their usefulness, often end up as scapegoats.
State television in some countries goes so far as to broadcast material to encourage an end to the practice.
The mayor of Congo's capital, Brazzaville, recently warned young people who prey on old people, sometimes killing them, to stop or face the consequences.

Congo's deputy minister for social matters, Melanie Ibouritso, told a news conference on Tuesday the government would conduct a census of old people in January as part of efforts to ensure that they are properly cared for.
